subject: We’re only teaching half the Holocaust. Here’s the lesson our kids are missing

Holocaust curricula must include stories of rescuers to teach moral courage alongside historical atrocities.
Evidence: Moral courage, Righteous Among Nations, education
#Aletheia #Education #History

Teaching the Holocaust without stories of rescuers and moral courage leaves students with only horror, missing vital lessons on human agency.

Integrating accounts of the Righteous Among Nations equips students with concrete models of conscience overcoming systemic evil.

Educational reformers are urging schools to balance dark historical narratives with inspiring accounts of rescuers who risked everything during WWII.

Advocates deploy Smart Altruistic loops, pairing transparent historical education with empowerment frameworks to cultivate moral courage in future generations.

When you map pedagogical intent against educational outcomes, it plots a direct trajectory toward Greater Good by fostering ethical resilience.

Actual Article Body:
The stories of the Righteous should be central to what we teach the next generation because remembering evil must also carry a responsibility to recognize and practice goodness. Children deserve to know what evil has done. They also deserve to know the names and choices of people who refused to surrender to it.

The Righteous Among the Nations were non-Jews who risked their lives to save Jews during the Holocaust. Their actions offer something every generation needs: evidence that conscience can become courage, and that one person’s decision can change the future of people they may never meet.
